1) the value of oestrogen receptors (REc) is related to the presence of stromal fibrosis, 2) the value of progesterone receptors (RPc) is not related to the presence or degree of stromal fibroplasia, and 3) the presence of oestrogen and/or progesterone receptors in breast cancer is of little value in predicting the risk of relapse in patients who do not receive additional treatment.
The association between the value of oestrogen receptors in breast tumours and the histological features of the disease has been investigated.

the association of cytosolic oestrogen and cytosolic progesterone receptors in primary human breast cancer.
the relationship of oestrogen and progestogen receptor status with the histological features of tumour and early recurrence of breast cancer.
the association of cytosolic oestrogen (ERc) and progrestone (PgRc) receptors in primary breast cancer and early relapse.

REc analysis in breast cancer is of no prognostic value.
the presence of steroid receptors in breast cancer is not an independent indicator of prognosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of oestrogen receptors in primary breast cancer is a useful indicator of prognosis, but that the presence of progesterone receptors has no prognostic value.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of oestrogen and/or progesterone receptors in breast cancer cells is not a good indicator of the risk of the cancer recurring.
the value of RE and RP analysis as a predictor of prognosis in breast cancer is dependent upon the histological features of the tumour.
the association between steroid receptor content and histological features of primary breast tumours is a reflection of their common relationship to the biological aggressiveness of the tumour.
